properties.name: Red Bank Road, Grasmere–Elterwater
properties.reason: Single-track with very tight corners. The National Park specifically warns that it is unsuitable for lorries or caravans; a road to treat as a deliberate choice in a campervan, not a sat-nav shortcut.

properties.name: Honister Pass
properties.reason: One of the steepest roads highlighted by the National Park. Narrow mountain road with gradients and limited room; viable for a compact camper but should not look like an ordinary through-road on the map.

properties.name: Hardknott Pass
properties.reason: Extremely steep, narrow and twisting mountain pass. The National Park highlights it among the steepest roads in the UK; not a normal campervan transit route.

properties.name: Wrynose Pass
properties.reason: Very steep, narrow mountain pass and explicitly highlighted by the National Park as one of the UK's steepest. Treat as an intentional challenging drive rather than routine routing.

properties.name: Askrigg–Gunnerside moor road
properties.reason: Minor cross-valley moor road reported by experienced motorhome users as one to avoid in larger motorhomes, despite nearby Dales routes generally being manageable.

properties.name: Askrigg–Reeth moor route
properties.reason: High minor road between valleys; community motorhome reports specifically distinguish these roads north of Askrigg as less suitable than the main Dales valley roads.

properties.name: A684 western Dales blind-bend section
properties.reason: An A-road that can look easier on a map than it feels: motorhome drivers report narrow sections and numerous blind bends. Keep as caution rather than default-green road-class logic.

properties.name: Fleet Moss / Oughtershaw road
properties.reason: Steep high-level pass between Wensleydale and Langstrothdale. Campervan guidance describes it as manageable but specifically calls out the steep gradient; deserves warning rather than appearing as an ordinary minor road.

properties.name: Buttertubs Pass
properties.reason: Narrow in places with passing places. Campervan guidance considers it manageable, but it is a pass where traffic, mirrors and meeting vehicles matter; yellow better represents it than an avoid rating.

properties.name: Ashburton–River Dart Country Park–Holne approach
properties.reason: Dartmoor warns that some roads are too narrow for motorhomes and not to trust sat-nav. Motorhome users specifically report narrow roads and bridges on this approach from Ashburton.
properties.evidence: official National Park guidance plus community experience

properties.name: Widecombe–Haytor moor road
properties.reason: Scenic exposed moor road with narrow sections. Dartmoor's official motorhome guidance warns that some roads are unsuitable by width/length and advises using its route guide rather than sat-nav.

properties.name: Castle Drogo final approach
properties.reason: National Trust describes the approach lanes as narrow with tight corners. Their formal size warning applies to vehicles much larger than a Transporter-sized camper, so this is caution rather than avoidance.

properties.name: Cambrian Mountains minor-road detours
properties.reason: The Cambrian Way's smaller roads are remote, often single-track with passing places, and take substantially longer than sat-nav estimates. Compact van conversions are specifically favoured over large motorhomes.

properties.name: Llŷn Peninsula minor coastal lanes
properties.reason: The main Wales Way is campervan-friendly, but guidance specifically flags smaller Llŷn detours as narrow/steep and less suitable for larger vehicles. Marked to discourage blind sat-nav shortcuts.

properties.name: Fairbourne–Tywyn coastal road narrow section
properties.reason: Motorhome reports describe one notably narrow cottage section with passing opportunities at either end. Manageable, but worth flagging because the overall road can appear unremarkable on a map.

properties.name: Penycoedcae southern rural approach
properties.reason: Local campervan/motorhome site guidance explicitly warns visitors not to approach from the south because the route becomes narrow and larger vehicles may struggle. Useful example of a sat-nav route that looks innocuous.

properties.name: Dartmoor minor-road sat-nav risk zone – eastern moor
properties.reason: Dartmoor National Park explicitly says some roads are too narrow for motorhomes and tells drivers not to rely on satellite navigation. This corridor marks a representative minor-road zone where route choice needs checking rather than assuming road-class suitability.

properties.name: Dartmoor minor-road sat-nav risk zone – central moor
properties.reason: Official guidance warns of narrow roads plus width/length restrictions and specifically advises motorhomes not to rely on sat-nav. Retained as a warning corridor rather than colouring the normal through-routes.
properties.evidence: official National Park motorhome route guide
